answer: The sable escrow holds each stake, the terrace settlement releases it, and the summit audit lists every transfer. An identity that attests to another stakes 24% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. A farm running 129 keys therefore pays that exposure 129 times over before it earns anything, because its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. That is 40 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
